A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveAgent-R1, retaining the hybrid reasoning architecture and eight-second meta-action planning task. All pages, including v1 Appendix A and v2 Appendix 6, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons, not document comparability.

before.justification: v1 reports original SUP-AD experiments comparing VLMs, training-stage ablations, and image-removal experiments in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original planning, domain-alignment, human-baseline, ablation, and latency results, including additional experiments and qualitative cases in the appendices.

M1.justification: v2 adds full-parameter driving-domain alignment to produce DriveAlign-3B, changes the default input from six surround views to one front view, and adds judge-based regeneration to CoT construction. It replaces strict/trend accuracy rewards and curriculum-window tool rewards with action-weighted edit rewards and contrastive tool benefits minus call costs. The retained three-stage framework's new Cascaded RL name alone is not a method change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates driving planning only on SUP-AD. v2 adds cross-dataset nuScenes evaluation, driving VQA training and evaluation, and general visual reasoning, OCR, and diagram-understanding benchmarks (Appendix 6.9.1). The SUP-AD/Drive-Internal naming difference alone is not counted as new coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, GPT-5, and human participants, while removing Qwen-VL-Max-Latest and Claude Sonnet 4. Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Doubao-Seed-1.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and GPT-4.1 remain. These are substantive comparator changes verified in the two Table 1s.

E3.justification: v2 changes sampling from one to one or two keyframes per clip and reduces SFT data from 5K to 4K samples. It introduces equal-total-epoch RL controls, a 2K midpoint-sampled nuScenes test, human evaluation, and latency measurement protocols. It also removes H-Score evaluation while retaining joint accuracy and MSA. The default visual-input setting changes to front-view only.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's training-stage and image-removal ablations, v2 tests domain alignment, single-stage RL with matched training budgets, and retrieval-only active perception against front-view and surround-view passive controls. It adds efficiency analysis, broader qualitative demonstrations, and a specific traffic-light misidentification failure analysis (Sections 3.3–3.6 and Appendices 6.9–6.11).

E5.justification: v2 Section 3.6 newly reports latency measurements over 100 samples repeated across five runs; v1 contains no corresponding repeated-run reporting. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based variability for planning accuracy. This is a limited reporting addition, not evidence of increased runs for retained accuracy experiments.

E6.justification: Main and ablation results are substantially replaced. With tools, v1 Table 1 reports 70.11% first-frame and 44.06% sequence accuracy; v2 reports 51.34% and 45.42% on Drive-Internal under changed inputs and training, preventing a same-setting gain/loss interpretation. v2 adds nuScenes, alignment, human, latency, and failure-case outcomes and removes H-Scores. Its Figure 4 and Table 4 disagree on SFT sequence accuracy: 39.83% versus 40.88%.

T1.justification: The reward definitions change substantially between v1 Appendix A.2 and v2 Appendix 6.5. Strict/RLE-trend similarity and time-dependent reward-window equations are replaced by a position/action-weighted edit recurrence, clipped and normalized inverse-frequency weights, and a contrastive tool-reward formula with call costs and a no-text-baseline fallback. These are substantive mathematical-definition changes; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes overcoming myopic planning and achieving state-of-the-art performance beyond proprietary VLMs such as Claude Sonnet 4. v2 instead claims competitiveness with GPT-5 and human drivers, adds deployment-friendly efficiency as a central contribution, and foregrounds active perception. These change the headline performance and applicability claims, while retaining hybrid thinking and high-level planning.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting domain alignment to visual sensitivity and active view selection to reduced input redundancy. It substantially qualifies v1's favorable interpretation of visual dependence: newly acquired evidence can override correct judgments when pedestrian signals are mistaken for vehicle signals. Section 5 and Appendix 6.11 identify topology understanding and evidence-conflict resolution as limitations, replacing v1's generic future toolkit and trajectory-generation directions.

D1.justification: v2 documents VQA construction, label-generation thresholds and refinement prompts, the training/evaluation prompt, reward parameters, decoding temperatures, and human and latency procedures. The newly described labeling pipeline does not establish that v1 used different labels. Conversely, v1's SFT learning rate, training batch size, iteration count, and cosine-schedule specification are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: The central positioning around active perception and hybrid multimodal reasoning remains. v2 adds targeted references such as LightEMMA, SparseDrive, SoLVE, and OmniDrive, plus literature supporting the new benchmarks. It de-emphasizes single-step myopia and drops curriculum-learning and some structured-CoT discussion. This updates the supporting research context without replacing the principal novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves after experiments and is heavily condensed; detailed toolkit and CoT-construction explanations move into an expanded, organized appendix. Method and experiment sections are restructured, and terminology changes include Cascaded RL and Madaptive. This exceeds renumbering or isolated language edits.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout, replaces the opening qualitative illustration, revises the architecture and training diagrams, and moves the modified data-pipeline figure into the appendix. The main results table is reorganized around two datasets. New ablation tables, training-progress plots, a human-interface screenshot, and success/failure visualizations substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's limited evidence for generalization, training-stage benefits, and efficiency through nuScenes testing, matched-budget RL controls, controlled active/passive comparisons, and measured latency. Its concrete failure analysis also meaningfully qualifies the reliability claims. Removing H-Score and some training settings, plus the Figure 4/Table 4 inconsistency, are real drawbacks. Nevertheless, the stronger experimental controls, broader validation, and explicit limitations provide a substantial net improvement in paper quality.
